badge.note: the score used in E1 and E2

sentences.text: Earlier, a {metric}distribution distance{/} meant moving sand.
The experiments mainly use a cousin, built from pairs.
Each dot is a snapshot.
Average every distance across the two crowds, and double it.
Subtract the average distance within each crowd.
Zero means the same law.

formulas.tex: \text{E2: one point} = 21 \text{ numbers per snapshot: } \log_{10} \text{ energies of } \cu{\mathbf{u}} \text{ and } \cb{\mathbf{B}} \text{ in the shells } |\mathbf{k}| = 1, \dots, 10, \text{ and } 10\,H_C,\ \text{standardized};\ \ \text{E1: the state } (Q, D, V),\ 3000 \text{ points}

\ck{\mathcal{E}}(P_1, P_2) = 2\,\mathbb{E}\|X - Y\| - \mathbb{E}\|X - X'\| - \mathbb{E}\|Y - Y'\|,\quad X, X' \sim P_1,\ \ Y, Y' \sim P_2 \text{ independent};\quad \ck{\mathcal{E}}(P_1, P_2) = 0 \iff P_1 = P_2

\mathbb{E}\big[\hat{\ck{\mathcal{E}}}_n\big] = \ck{\mathcal{E}}(P_1, P_2) + \big(\mathbb{E}\|X - X'\| + \mathbb{E}\|Y - Y'\|\big)/n > 0 \ \text{(all pairs, diagonal included): compare with the floor, never with zero};\ \ \ck{\mathcal{E}} = 2\,\mathrm{MMD}^2 \text{ for the distance kernel}

scenes.title: The least-distorting correction

badge.note: Prop. 7 · exact on the sample, when β* exists

toy.what: r = dE/dt = P - eps of one snapshot; true law mu = sum p_k N(m_k, s_k^2) (mean exactly 0: the energy budget); model q = law of r + bias; constants from assets/interactif/contrainte-loi.js (formula 1 and slider default b = 0.4)
toy.dots: x_j = F_mu^-1((j - 0.5)/n) + bias, j = 1..n (deterministic quantiles; F_mu^-1 by bisection on the exact CDF)

alternatives.label: drop the top
alternatives.rule: uniform weights on the lowest k dots, one fractional weight at the boundary, so that the weighted mean is exactly 0

alternatives.label: linear
alternatives.rule: w proportional to max(0, 1 - a r), a > 0 by bisection so that the weighted mean is exactly 0

params.cost: KL(w || uniform) = sum_i w_i log(n w_i), with 0 log 0 = 0; bars proportional, no digits
params.tilt: w proportional to exp(beta r), beta < 0 by Newton on log sum exp(beta r_i) (contrainte-loi.js formula 4); assert in setup that its cost is the smallest of the three (Proposition 7 on the sample), Scene.warn otherwise

sentences.text: Reweighting, up close.
The {model}model's{/} crowd misses its target average.
Leave every snapshot in place; change only how much each counts.
Many weightings hit the target.
The least distorting one is an exponential tilt, known as the I-projection.
Picture crowds as points: those with the right average lie on a line.
The tilted crowd is the foot of the perpendicular.
Any other fix pays the tilt's cost plus an extra, as in Pythagoras.
And nothing moves: the tilted crowd lives only where the model's crowd was.

labels: energy change of one snapshot · r = dE/dt
no snapshot moves · only its weight
cost: how much the crowd is distorted
no dot here: no mass, before or after

formulas.tex: \operatorname{supp}\cm{q}^{*} = \operatorname{supp}\cm{q};\ \ \text{on samples: } w_i \propto e^{\boldsymbol\beta\cdot\mathbf{g}(x_i)},\ \textstyle\sum_i w_i = 1;\ \ \boldsymbol\beta^{*} \text{ exists only if } \mathbf{c} \text{ lies inside the convex hull of the values of } \mathbf{g}

sources: en/rapport/index.qmd:462 (the identities must be enforced at the distribution level; two routes: tilt the generated distribution afterwards, or modify the training)

en/rapport/index.qmd:465-472 (Proposition 7: among the distributions absolutely continuous with respect to q whose mean of g is c, the closest to q in KL is the tilted distribution e^{β*·g} q / Z(β*), β* minimizing the convex dual log Z(β) - β·c; I-projection due to Csiszár 1975; on a sample, self-normalized weights w_i ∝ e^{β·g(x_i)}, ESS = 1/Σ w_i²; a reweighting does not create mass: the support of the tilted law is that of q)
en/rapport/index.qmd:474-482 (proof; Pythagorean identity KL(ν||q) = KL(ν||ν*) + KL(ν*||q) ≥ KL(ν*||q), equality only for ν = ν*; the support cannot grow)
en/rapport/index.qmd:485 (β* exists only if c lies inside the convex hull of the values of g under q)
en/rapport/index.qmd:1477 (bibliography: Csiszár 1975, Annals of Probability 3(1), 146-158, DOI 10.1214/aop/1176996454)
en/these/index.qmd:579 (exponential tilting is the minimal correction in the Kullback-Leibler sense, but it does not create mass)

sentences.text: How much is left of a reweighted crowd?
Its {metric}effective sample size{/} says.
Equal weights: the whole crowd.
One giant weight: one person.
On the flat sheet, at the smallest test {param}eta{/}, the poll keeps ninety-nine percent.
At the three largest, it bottoms out: one snapshot in five hundred.
Rank the values by how far the {model}model's{/} budget was off: the poll shrinks in nearly the same order.
Where the poll survives, little needed fixing.
Where much needed fixing, it collapses.
On the three dials, too, reweighting improved no crowd: one snapshot weighed thirty-three times the average.

how far the base model's energy budget was off

sentences.text: Picture a {model}model{/} that never visits the bridge between the two polarities, where every crossing happens.
Can reweighting bring back the {metric}crossing rate{/}?
No. Rice reads the rate inside the strip, and the strip is empty. Zero, times any weight, is zero.
Push harder, and the weight piles onto a few snapshots at the edge.
Reweighting cannot visit places the model never went.
The thesis plan's risk table agrees: reweighting alone is no fallback.

question.en: If the crowd loss fails, what is the *fallback*, since *reweighting* fails where the model is poor?
question.say: If the crowd loss fails, what is the fallback, since reweighting fails where the model is poor?
question.fr: Si la perte sur la foule échoue, quel est le *repli*, puisque la *repondération* échoue là où le modèle est mauvais ?
question.why: The plan's tier-0 stopping rule falls back on reweighting, yet its risk table says reweighting alone is no fallback: it improved no crowd in E1 or E2, and in E2 kept one effective snapshot in 500 where the model was poorest.
question.unblocks: The tier-0 and tier-1 stopping rules and ablations; whether to budget anchored fine-tuning (proximity term, ramp of the loss weight, three seeds) instead; ESS/N as a reported diagnostic.
question.why_fr: La règle d'arrêt du palier 0 se replie sur la repondération, mais la table des risques du plan dit que la repondération seule n'est pas un repli : elle n'a amélioré aucune foule dans E1 ni dans E2, et dans E2 elle ne gardait qu'un échantillon effectif sur 500 là où le modèle était le plus mauvais.
question.unblocks_fr: Les règles d'arrêt et les ablations des paliers 0 et 1 ; le choix de budgéter plutôt un affinage ancré (terme de proximité, montée progressive du poids de la perte, trois graines) ; l'ESS/N comme diagnostic rapporté.
